_comment: Publicly-readable GitHub resources we inspected for this competition. URLs are public; summaries and extracted_ideas are our own notes. relevance_score in [0,1] = how directly it informs our learned-graph path. No private scraping.

sources.title: Cell-tracking competition metric specification
sources.summary: Official scoring formula: final = max(0, edge_jaccard * (1 - 0.1*(T_pred - T_true)/T_true)) + 0.1*division_jaccard. Nodes matched to GT by <=7um centroid bipartite matching; edges are TP only when both endpoints match GT-connected nodes AND span a unit timepoint; divisions are out-degree-2 sources with +/-1 timepoint tolerance; micro-averaged across samples.
extracted_ideas: node over-prediction penalty coeff 0.1 on T_pred excess

sources.title: evaluate.py scoring entrypoint
sources.summary: Reference scoring driver: loads GT and prediction graphs, runs node matching then edge/division jaccard, applies the node-count penalty, and micro-averages. Confirms the exact order of operations behind metrics.md.
extracted_ideas: penalty applied to the edge term, not the division term

sources.title: tracking_cellmot/metrics.py
sources.summary: Implementation of edge_jaccard and the node-count penalty. Shows edges keyed by matched-GT endpoint pairs and that a non-unit-timepoint edge is not credited.
extracted_ideas: edge TP requires both endpoints matched to GT-connected nodes
penalty term computed from predicted vs true node counts

sources.title: tracking_cellmot/division_metrics.py
sources.summary: Division jaccard implementation: a division is an out-degree-2 source; matched to GT with +/-1 timepoint tolerance. Motivates safe-division recovery as a direct lever on the 0.1-weighted division term.

sources.title: lb893 learned-graph tracker with micro-safe divisions
sources.summary: Public 0.893 solution. Uses the IDENTICAL predict command to our M16 (det 0.99, ilp-edge -1.0, appearance/disappearance 0.1, division 1.0, --use-ilp). The 0.874 -> 0.893 gain is entirely post-GEFF processing: safe divisions, single/two-frame gap recovery with synthetic nodes, line-fit smoothing, isolated-node pruning.
extracted_ideas: ILP weights are NOT the lever (same command as ours)
gap recovery with synthetic intermediate nodes

sources.title: gap2 velocity ablation
sources.summary: Velocity-gated two-frame gap recovery ablation: bridge a tracklet end at t to a start at t+3 with two synthetic nodes, gated on per-step distance and velocity consistency (direction cosine + magnitude). Directly implementable as our gap2 op.
extracted_ideas: two-frame gap = two synthetic nodes at t+1,t+2

sources.title: nms38 candidate
sources.summary: Non-max-suppression density technique on the CLASSICAL-detection (non-learned) path, capped around 0.839. NOT applicable to our learned-graph pipeline; kept as a negative/known-ceiling reference.

sources.title: top notebooks analysis

extracted_ideas: post-processing is the differentiator among top scores
division and gap handling recur across top notebooks

sources.title: biohub-cell-tracking-v4-unet-ilp-reproduction (public high-score notebook)
sources.summary: Public notebook that runs the SAME 400ep artifact (artifact_name contains '400ep', weight_sha256 12f6881ee3620a831697ca098ff8f48e687a24225f4e048b538deec3562fe771; RAW base 127790 nodes / 115694 edges) we tested in M24, but reaches a much higher public score by REPLACING our thin safe_div/gap/linefit postprocess with a richer evaluator-safe OUTPUT pipeline: motion_relink_edges (per-frame Hungarian on motion-predicted distance + edge_prob bonus) -> close_single_frame_gaps (reuse-or-insert) -> add_safe_divisions_postlink -> apply_edge_policy_veto (embedded logistic edge-only policy, capped 1%, skip divisions) -> filter_short_track_components (min_len 7, keep divisions) -> linefit_smooth. Its public output: final 119763 node rows / 115080 edge rows / 234843 submission rows. We reproduce the LOGIC hidden-safe (never the static submission.csv) as M27.
extracted_ideas: M24 underperformed on 400ep because postprocess was too thin (safe_div/gap/linefit only)
motion_relink: per-frame Hungarian assignment replaces raw learned edges (in<=1/out<=1 skeleton)
edge-policy VETO (conservative, capped at 1%, skip division sources) trims false-positive edges
filter_short_track_components lowers the node penalty; keep components that contain divisions

sources.title: biohub_winning_strategy.md (uploaded)
sources.summary: Uploaded winning-strategy analysis arguing our post-processing is too CONSERVATIVE: gap caps too small, division-recovery cap too small, det-threshold 0.99 possibly too high; recommends building a local CV before blind LB tuning and pursuing RECALL-oriented edge/gap/division recovery as the path beyond M19-C 0.880. Basis for the M28 metric-aware recall-expansion pack.
extracted_ideas: gap1/gap2 caps in M19-C are too small - many TP gaps left unrecovered
division-recovery cap too small - the division term may be underused
det-threshold 0.99 may be too high - sweep down (0.95 first, then 0.90/0.80)
add gap3 (three-frame) recovery for high-upside recall
linefit smoothing may hurt curved motion - test disabling it
build local CV before blind LB tuning
